title: Butuan City declared under state of calamity due to water crisis

blocks.text: BUTUAN CITY – This region’s frontier and capital city Butuan has been declared under a state of calamity due to water shortage for almost three weeks now. Because of the severe water problem, 91,425 families, or more than of its 269,000 residents, have been experiencing almost no-water service as water availability have continued to decline, particularly in the city's 11 most-populated barangays. Accordingly, the water shortage was linked to the prevailing dry spell in this capital city of Caraga region, which has experience a significant rainfall deficit. Butuan City Mayor Lawrence Lemuel “Law” H. Fortun ordered the implementation of water rationing in most affected areas, but these interventions have remainedinsufficient as the shortage continued. Fortun now centered the use of 30-percentQuick Response Fund to the most affected barangays. The state of calamity declaration is expected to allow the city government and affected barangays to mobilize additional resources and access Quick Response Funds for emergency measures, including the provision and installation of water tanks, tankers, pumps and filtration systems, as well as other equipment needed for water distribution and rationing. The state of calamity was declared over the weekend, during the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) Third Special Session, the approval of SP Resolution No. 17-444-2026 at the City Hal Conference Room here. “The resolution was approved as the continuing water shortage has significantly affected residents’ access to water across several barangays,” the SP Resolution said. “We are doing our very best to address this problem,” Mayor Fortun said. The water crisis comes as Agusan del Norte and Butuan City, continues to experience a significant rainfall deficit. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) placed the province under “Dry Spell” status as of August 23, 2026.
